title: Lost Comms: AVEF & MEA

faa.title: IFR operations: Two-way radio communications failure

hook: The radio just died in the clouds. What now?

scenes.narration: Thirty seconds, kid. Your radio quits in I M C. The reg is ninety-one one eighty-five, and it answers two questions: where do I go, and how high.
First — if you break out into V F R, stay V F R and land. Reg's over, lesson's over, go buy a handheld radio.
Still in the soup? Route: A V E F. Fly what you were Assigned. Being vectored? Go direct to what the Vector was for. Otherwise what ATC said to Expect. Last resort — what you Filed.
Altitude: fly the HIGHEST of three, for each route segment. Minimum enroute altitude, what you were told to Expect, or what you were Assigned. Highest. The rocks don't negotiate.
V F R? Land. I M C? Route A V E F, altitude highest of M E A, expected, assigned. Squawk seventy-six hundred and keep flying the airplane — it doesn't know the radio's dead.
It's all in ninety-one one eighty-five. Two paragraphs. Memorize both.

quiz.question: Lost comms in IMC. Route priority under 91.185 is:
quiz.explanation: AVEF: the route Assigned; if being Vectored, direct to the fix/route the vector was for; then Expected; then Filed.

quiz.question: Lost comms altitude for each segment is the HIGHEST of:
quiz.explanation: 91.185(c)(2): fly the highest of the minimum IFR altitude (MEA), the altitude ATC told you to expect, or your last assigned altitude.

quiz.question: Radio fails and you encounter VFR conditions. You should:
choices: Continue VFR and land as soon as practicable
Climb back into IMC and fly AVEF
quiz.explanation: 91.185(b): if you hit VFR conditions after the failure, remain VFR and land as soon as practicable.
